doc.code_a11y_desc: Follows WAI-ARIA guidelines with proper roles, labels, and keyboard navigation support.
doc.code_anatomy_content: The visual representation of the code string, formatted with mono font and syntax colors.
doc.code_anatomy_root: The container for the code snippet which handles inline or block rendering and Overflow behavior.
doc.code_best_practice_1: Keep code blocks short and focused on a single concept to maintain readability.
doc.code_best_practice_2: Use the block property for multi-line snippets and the highlightLines property (if supported) to draw attention to specific logic.
doc.code_choice_alt_when: When you need to render complex formatted text that includes more than just code (use a Markdown component).
doc.code_choice_matrix_desc: Select based on whether the code is part of a sentence (inline) or a standalone block.
doc.code_choice_self_when: For displaying technical values, function names, or snippets that require mono-font formatting.
doc.code_content_guideline: Ensure snippets are syntactically correct and use appropriate indentation for block displays.
doc.code_design_intent: Code is designed to provide clear, readable formatting for programming instructions and technical values. By using semantic HTML <code> or <pre> tags and specialized font tokens, it ensures technical content is visually distinguished from regular prose.
doc.code_long_desc: Used to display inline code or code blocks
doc.code_motion_desc: Uses minimal transitions for state changes, such as when switching horizontal scroll positions.
doc.code_note_desc:
> Code blocks in the Code component (when the block property is true) have horizontal scrolling enabled.
> This is because forcibly wrapping long lines of code breaks indentation and structure, reducing readability.
doc.code_responsive_desc: In block format, horizontal scrolling occurs according to the container width to prevent layout collapse.
doc.code_scenario_1: Display function names or commands inline within documentation.
doc.code_scenario_2: Display request/response logs in block format on admin screens.
doc.code_tokens_desc: Uses mono font tokens and applies background and border tokens according to inline/block formats.
doc.code_title: Component for displaying inline code or code blocks
doc.errorboundary_a11y_desc: Follows WAI-ARIA guidelines with proper roles, labels, and keyboard navigation support.
doc.errorboundary_anatomy_content: The fallback UI components (like a heading and retry button) that are displayed when an error is caught.
doc.errorboundary_anatomy_root: The wrapper that intercepts React lifecycle errors and prevents them from bubbling up to the entire application.
doc.errorboundary_best_practice_1: Wrap large, independent sections of your app (like sidebars or feature modules) so a single failure doesn't crash the entire UI.
doc.errorboundary_best_practice_2: Provide a clear 'Try Again' button that restarts the failed process rather than just showing a static error message.
doc.errorboundary_choice_alt_when: For simple form validation errors where a FieldError or Alert is more appropriate.
doc.errorboundary_choice_matrix_desc: Select based on the size of the component tree you wish to protect.
doc.errorboundary_choice_self_when: For critical UI segments or third-party integrations that might throw unexpected runtime exceptions.
doc.errorboundary_content_guideline: The error message should be non-technical and helpful, guiding the user towards recovery.
doc.errorboundary_custom_desc: By providing fallback as a function, you can freely customize the error message and reset button.
doc.errorboundary_def_desc: Displays a default error UI with a "Try again" button.
doc.errorboundary_design_intent: ErrorBoundary acts as a safety net for the application. It gracefully handles unexpected runtime crashes in the component tree, providing users with a meaningful 'safe state' and a way to recover (retry) instead of a blank screen or a broken UI.
doc.errorboundary_feat_1_desc: Prevents the entire app from crashing due to the failure of a single component.
doc.errorboundary_feat_2_desc: You can provide your own fallback UI or use the default one.
doc.errorboundary_feat_3_desc: Includes a reset mechanism to retry rendering of child elements.
doc.errorboundary_long_desc: The ErrorBoundary component catches JavaScript errors that occur anywhere in its child component tree, logs those errors, and displays a fallback UI instead of the crashed component tree.
doc.errorboundary_motion_desc: Features smooth fading transitions when swapping the broken content with the fallback UI.
doc.errorboundary_scenario_1: Wrapping dynamic charts or third-party widgets that might throw unexpected errors.
doc.errorboundary_scenario_2: Protecting the main dashboard view from failures in auxiliary data providers.
doc.errorboundary_title: Boundary element to catch runtime errors and show fallback UI
doc.fielderror_a11y_desc: Follows WAI-ARIA guidelines with proper roles, labels, and keyboard navigation support.
doc.fielderror_anatomy_content: The error message string that explains the validation failure to the user.
doc.fielderror_anatomy_root: The typographic container that often includes an icon and uses a thematic 'error' color to draw attention.
doc.fielderror_best_practice_1: Place error messages directly below the corresponding input to maintain proximity and context.
doc.fielderror_best_practice_2: Avoid long paragraphs; use concise fragments like 'Required field' or 'Invalid email format' for quick scanning.
doc.fielderror_choice_alt_when: When you need to display multiple errors affecting the entire form at once (use Alert instead).
doc.fielderror_choice_matrix_desc: Select based on whether the error is tied to a specific input or a broader context.
doc.fielderror_choice_self_when: For providing validation feedback directly adjacent to a form control.
doc.fielderror_content_guideline: Be helpful and specific. Tell the user exactly what is wrong and how to fix it (e.g., 'Passwords must be at least 8 characters').
doc.fielderror_design_intent: FieldError provides clear, immediate feedback when user input doesn't meet validation criteria. It uses consistent typography and color to signal that a correction is required in a specific form field.
doc.fielderror_motion_desc: Uses a subtle 'slide-down' or 'fade-in' animation to indicate the appearance of new validation feedback.
doc.fielderror_scenario_1: Validation feedback for a registration form with complex requirements.
doc.fielderror_scenario_2: Inline error display for real-time search filtering.
doc.fieldset_a11y_desc: Follows WAI-ARIA guidelines with proper roles, labels, and keyboard navigation support.
doc.fieldset_anatomy_content: A group of related form controls (inputs, labels, errors) that are logically separated from other form sections.
doc.fieldset_anatomy_root: The semantic container that provides a accessible border and legend for a group of inputs.
doc.fieldset_best_practice_1: Use Fieldset to group related options like 'Personal Information' or 'Payment Details' to improve form structure.
doc.fieldset_best_practice_2: Always include a descriptive legend to provide a clear label for the grouped inputs for screen reader users.
doc.fieldset_choice_alt_when: When the components are visually grouped but have no logical or semantic relation (use a Box or Stack instead).
doc.fieldset_choice_matrix_desc: Select based on the complexity of the form and the need for semantic grouping.
doc.fieldset_choice_self_when: For logical grouping of inputs that belong to the same category.
doc.fieldset_content_guideline: Legends should be short and act as a group title (e.g., 'Address').
doc.fieldset_design_intent: Fieldset is used to group related fields in a form, providing both a visual boundary and semantic structure. This is critical for complex forms, as it helps users (and screen readers) understand the context of a set of inputs (e.g., 'Shipping Address').
doc.fieldset_motion_desc: Typically uses static layouts, but supports smooth opacity transitions if the entire group is toggled.
doc.fieldset_scenario_1: Grouping radio buttons or checkboxes that belong to the same configuration category.
doc.fieldset_scenario_2: Nesting address fields (Street, City, Zip) within a larger checkout form.
doc.focustrap_a11y_desc: Follows WAI-ARIA guidelines with proper roles, labels, and keyboard navigation support.
doc.focustrap_anatomy_content: The container for interactive elements (such as buttons or inputs) that the user should be able to tab through.
doc.focustrap_anatomy_root: The wrapper component that monitors focus events and prevents the focus from leaving the defined boundary.
doc.focustrap_auto_focus_desc: Setting the autoFocus prop to true shifts focus to the first focusable element as soon as the trap becomes active.
doc.focustrap_best_practice_1: Ensure that the user has a clear way to exit the trap, such as a close button or pressing the Escape key.
doc.focustrap_best_practice_2: Only activate the trap when necessary (e.g., when a Modal is open) to avoid confusing users with unexpected focus behavior.
doc.focustrap_choice_alt_when: When you only need to focus a single element once on mount (use a standard autoFocus property instead).
doc.focustrap_choice_matrix_desc: Select based on whether focus needs to be restricted (locked) or just initialized.
doc.focustrap_choice_self_when: For Modals, Dialogs, or any temporary overlay where the user must complete a sub-task.
doc.focustrap_content_guideline: Ensure there is at least one focusable element inside the trap to avoid soft-locking the keyboard navigation.
doc.focustrap_design_intent: FocusTrap is designed to ensure that users navigating via keyboard remain focused on a specific task or interactive zone, such as a modal or dropdown. This prevents users from accidentally interacting with background elements, which is a critical requirement for WCAG compliance and overall usability.
doc.focustrap_feat_1: Restricts Tab key movement within the component.
doc.focustrap_feat_2: Pressing Tab at the last element returns focus to the first, and pressing Shift + Tab at the first element moves it to the last (loop).
doc.focustrap_feat_3: When the component mounts (or becomes active), it can automatically shift focus to the first focusable element inside.
doc.focustrap_feat_4: When the component unmounts, it restores focus to the previously active element.
doc.focustrap_long_desc: FocusTrap is a utility component designed to trap keyboard focus within a specific area. It is used to implement accessible UIs such as modals, dialogs, and drawers where you want to restrict user interaction to a specific range.
doc.focustrap_motion_desc: Works silently in the background without its own visual motion, typically accompanying a Modal's opening animation.
doc.focustrap_scenario_1: Modals and Dialogs where the user must complete a task before returning to the main page.
doc.focustrap_scenario_2: Managing navigation within a side drawer or navigation overlay.
doc.focustrap_title: Utility to keep keyboard focus within a specific area
doc.highlight_long_desc: The Highlight component emphasizes specific parts of a text using the mark tag.
doc.highlight_title: Component to visually emphasize specific keywords in text
doc.kbd_a11y_desc: Follows WAI-ARIA guidelines with proper roles, labels, and keyboard navigation support.
doc.kbd_anatomy_content: The character or key name (e.g., 'Enter', '⌘') representing the physical keyboard key.
doc.kbd_anatomy_root: The typographic container that mimics the look of a physical key with specific border and shadow styles.
doc.kbd_best_practice_1: Use Kbd for actual physical key presses. For software concepts or commands, consider using Code instead.
doc.kbd_best_practice_2: Combine multiple Kbd elements with a plus (+) sign or space to represent complex multi-key combinations.
doc.kbd_choice_alt_when: When representing data values or code snippets that aren't specifically triggered by physical keys (use Code instead).
doc.kbd_choice_matrix_desc: Select based on whether you are showing a shortcut (Kbd) or general technical text.
doc.kbd_choice_self_when: For documenting hotkeys, shortcuts, or required hardware button presses.
doc.kbd_combined_desc: Multiple Kbd components can be combined to represent shortcuts.
doc.kbd_content_guideline: Use symbols for common keys (e.g., ⌘, ⇧, ↵) to save space and improve recognition.
doc.kbd_design_intent: Kbd is used to visually highlight keyboard interactions or shortcuts. It uses a 'key cap' style to make it immediately obvious that the text refers to a physical input action rather than regular content.
doc.kbd_long_desc: An inline component used to indicate keyboard shortcuts, individual keys, or keyboard input.
doc.kbd_motion_desc: Uses a subtle 'press' effect transition if used within an interactive list of shortcuts.
doc.kbd_scenario_1: Documenting keyboard shortcuts for a productivity app (e.g., ⌘ + K for search).
doc.kbd_scenario_2: Indicating the key used to trigger a specific game action or UI shortcut.
doc.kbd_size_desc: You can adjust the size using the `size` property.
doc.marquee_a11y_desc: Follows WAI-ARIA guidelines with proper roles, labels, and keyboard navigation support.
doc.marquee_anatomy_content: The collection of content items (text, logos, icons) being animated in a loop.
doc.marquee_anatomy_root: The overflow-hidden container that defines the scroll window and manages the animation timing.
doc.marquee_best_practice_1: Use Marquee for non-critical information that benefits from passive visibility, such as news headlines or community logos.
doc.marquee_best_practice_2: Provide a 'pause on hover' mechanism to allow users to read specific content at their own pace.
doc.marquee_choice_alt_when: When the user needs to interact with specific items frequently (use a Carousel or Grid instead).
doc.marquee_choice_matrix_desc: Select based on the desired level of energy and visual movement in the header or footer section.
doc.marquee_choice_self_when: For displaying continuous loops of logos, headlines, or brand messages.
doc.marquee_content_guideline: Items should have consistent heights to ensure a smooth scrolling experience.
doc.marquee_design_intent: Marquee provides an eye-catching loop animation for content. It's ideal for news tickers, logo scrolls, or highlighting sponsors in a way that encourages passive scanning by the user.
doc.marquee_motion_desc: Features a smooth, framerate-independent scrolling animation. Values can be adjusted for speed and direction.
doc.marquee_scenario_1: A scrolling list of brand logos at the bottom of a landing page.
doc.marquee_scenario_2: Real-time news or stock price ticker at the top of a financial dashboard.
doc.qrcode_a11y_desc: Follows WAI-ARIA guidelines with proper roles, labels, and keyboard navigation support.
doc.qrcode_anatomy_content: The procedurally generated matrix and patterns representing the encoded data.
doc.qrcode_anatomy_root: The container that handles scaling, background colors, and optional logo overlays for the QR code.
doc.qrcode_best_practice_1: Ensure high contrast between the dots and the background to maintain high readability across different scanning environments.
doc.qrcode_best_practice_2: Adjust the level of error correction if you include a large logo centerpiece to prevent scan failures.
doc.qrcode_choice_alt_when: When you only need to show a simple static image (use an Image component instead).
doc.qrcode_choice_matrix_desc: Select based on whether the data is dynamic (URL, JSON) or static text.
doc.qrcode_choice_self_when: For cross-device workflows where a user scans a link from their desktop to a mobile phone.
doc.qrcode_content_guideline: Avoid encoding extremely long strings; the more data you encode, the denser and harder to scan the QR code becomes.
doc.qrcode_desc_2: QRCode renders a specified string as a QR code. It supports output in SVG or Canvas format and allows customization of size, color, and error correction level.
doc.qrcode_design_intent: QRCode bridges the gap between digital and physical interactions. It allows users to quickly transfer URLs or data to mobile devices, ensuring accessibility for cross-device workflows.
doc.qrcode_long_desc: A component for displaying information as a QR code.
doc.qrcode_motion_desc: Can be combined with Fade-in transitions to reveal the code smoothly once generated.
doc.qrcode_scenario_1: Generating a scan-to-pay link at the end of a checkout process.
doc.qrcode_scenario_2: Sharing a Wi-Fi configuration or contact card in a user's profile view.
doc.qrcode_var_color_desc: Use bgColor and fgColor to change the background and foreground (dot) colors.
doc.qrcode_var_logo_desc: Use imageSettings to place a logo image in the center of the QR code.
doc.qrcode_var_size_desc: You can specify the width and height of the QR code with the size prop.
doc.scrollarea_a11y_desc: Follows WAI-ARIA guidelines with proper roles, labels, and keyboard navigation support.
doc.scrollarea_anatomy_content: The full-sized child content that can be panned or scrolled within the limited viewport.
doc.scrollarea_anatomy_root: The container that provides the fixed viewport and custom thematic scrollbars.
doc.scrollarea_best_practice_1: Use ScrollArea for internal regions with high content density, like file explorers or sidebar navigation menus.
doc.scrollarea_best_practice_2: Set a fixed height or max-height on the ScrollArea to trigger the custom scrollbar behavior.
doc.scrollarea_choice_alt_when: When browser-native scrollbars are sufficient or preferred for specific accessibility reasons (use a standard Box with overflow: auto instead).
doc.scrollarea_choice_matrix_desc: Select based on whether you need customized styling for the scrollbars or specific visibility controls.
doc.scrollarea_choice_self_when: For modern, theme-aware applications where native scrollbars feel out of place.
doc.scrollarea_content_guideline: Ensure children have enough padding to avoid content being clipped by the scrollbar track.
doc.scrollarea_design_intent: ScrollArea ensures that applications maintain a consistent visual style regardless of browser-specific scrollbar implementations. It provides a highly customizable, high-performance scrolling experience.
doc.scrollarea_motion_desc: Provides smooth, inertial scrolling on touch devices and gentle opacity fades for the scrollbar thumb.
doc.scrollarea_scenario_1: A long list of notifications in a compact dropdown menu.
doc.scrollarea_scenario_2: Sidebars in a code editor style interface where space is limited.
doc.scrollprogress_a11y_desc: Follows WAI-ARIA guidelines with proper roles, labels, and keyboard navigation support.
doc.scrollprogress_anatomy_content: The filled portion of the bar representing the percentage of content already scrolled.
doc.scrollprogress_anatomy_root: The container that tracks the scroll position of the target and calculates the width/height of the progress bar.
doc.scrollprogress_best_practice_1: Position the progress bar at the very top or bottom of the viewport for maximum visibility without obscuring content.
doc.scrollprogress_best_practice_2: Use subtle colors that match the brand theme but don't distract the user from reading the actual text.
doc.scrollprogress_choice_alt_when: When tracking the progress of an operation (e.g. upload) rather than scroll position (use Progress instead).
doc.scrollprogress_choice_matrix_desc: Select based on the orientation of your content (vertical vs horizontal scroll).
doc.scrollprogress_choice_self_when: For long-form reading experiences like articles, documentation, or legal terms.
doc.scrollprogress_content_guideline: The progress indicator should be non-intrusive; avoid using heavy borders or loud shadow effects.
doc.scrollprogress_design_intent: ScrollProgress provides a subtle visual cue about the length of a page and the user's current reading progress. It helps manage user expectations for long-form content like articles or documentation.
doc.scrollprogress_motion_desc: Uses a highly responsive, frame-locked transition to ensure the progress indicator tracks the scroll position without any perceptible lag.
doc.scrollprogress_scenario_1: Reading indicator for long blog articles or legal terms of service.
doc.scrollprogress_scenario_2: Vertical progress tracker for multi-page walkthroughs or documentation.
doc.transition_a11y_desc: Follows WAI-ARIA guidelines with proper roles, labels, and keyboard navigation support.
doc.transition_anatomy_content: The elements being animated during their mount or unmount lifecycle stages.
doc.transition_anatomy_root: The component that coordinates CSS class applications at various stages of the animation lifecycle (enter, leave).
doc.transition_best_practice_1: Keep durations short (150ms-300ms) to ensure the UI feels snappy and responsive rather than sluggish.
doc.transition_best_practice_2: Always account for reduced-motion settings to ensure accessibility for users who prefer minimal movement.
doc.transition_choice_alt_when: When the visibility change is instant and does not benefit from a staggered or smoothed animation (use standard conditional rendering instead).
doc.transition_choice_matrix_desc: Select based on the desired animation style (Fade, Scale, Slide).
doc.transition_choice_self_when: For enhancing the perceived quality of UI interactions like menu opening or item removal.
doc.transition_content_guideline: Avoid nesting many Transitions inside each other as it can lead to complex and hard-to-debug timing issues.
doc.transition_design_intent: Transition provides a declarative API for handling CSS animations. It ensures that complex state changes, like opening a menu or removing a list item, are visually smooth and follow systemic motion principles.
doc.transition_motion_desc: Enables the orchestration of complex CSS-based animations through various lifestyle stages (enter, active, done, exit).
doc.transition_scenario_1: Fading in a modal window when a user clicks a 'Details' button.
doc.transition_scenario_2: Sliding in a notification toast from the corner of the screen.
doc.visuallyhidden_a11y_desc: Follows WAI-ARIA guidelines with proper roles, labels, and keyboard navigation support.
doc.visuallyhidden_anatomy_content: The content that is hidden from the eye but exposed to assistive technologies.
doc.visuallyhidden_anatomy_root: The container that applies specific CSS clip and absolute positioning to hide content while keeping it in the DOM.
doc.visuallyhidden_best_practice_1: Use for labeling interactive elements that only have an icon, such as 'Add to cart' for a plus (+) button.
doc.visuallyhidden_best_practice_2: Ensure the hidden text is concise but descriptive enough to convey the full intent of the visual element.
doc.visuallyhidden_choice_alt_when: When the content should be completely ignored by both the user and screen readers (use an empty ARIA label or aria-hidden='true' instead).
doc.visuallyhidden_choice_matrix_desc: Select based on whether you need a permanent label (VisuallyHidden) or a temporary tooltip.
doc.visuallyhidden_choice_self_when: For providing 'screen reader only' context to graphical content.
doc.visuallyhidden_content_guideline: Hidden text should match the tone and terminology of visible labels to ensure a consistent experience for all users.
doc.visuallyhidden_design_intent: VisuallyHidden is a crucial accessibility tool. It provides descriptive text to screen readers for graphical actions (like an 'Edit' label on an icon-only button), ensuring that all users can understand the UI regardless of their visual ability.
doc.visuallyhidden_motion_desc: None. This component is invisible to the eye and does not participate in visual layout or motion.
doc.visuallyhidden_scenario_1: Providing a heading for a sidebar that is visually clear but requires an explicit H2 for screen readers.
doc.visuallyhidden_scenario_2: Hidden labels for decorative SVG elements that need to be ignored by some but described for others.
doc.code_keyboard_desc: Tab focuses the code block. If a copy button is present, Tab reaches it and Enter or Space copies the content.
doc.code_i18n_desc: All visible text uses i18n keys. Pass translated strings through the aria-label prop of the copy button.
doc.errorboundary_keyboard_desc: This component does not require specific keyboard interaction. Tab moves focus through any action buttons in the fallback UI.
doc.errorboundary_i18n_desc: All visible text uses i18n keys. Pass translated strings through the fallback content children.
doc.focustrap_keyboard_desc: Tab cycles focus through all focusable elements within the trap. Shift+Tab moves focus backward. Focus does not escape the trap boundaries while it is active.
doc.focustrap_i18n_desc: Apply i18n to the content placed inside the FocusTrap component.
doc.kbd_keyboard_desc: This component is a display element for showing keyboard key labels. It does not require specific keyboard interaction of its own.
doc.kbd_i18n_desc: All visible text uses i18n keys. Pass translated strings through the children prop.
doc.qrcode_keyboard_desc: This component does not require specific keyboard interaction. Provide a meaningful aria-label describing the QR code content for screen reader accessibility.
doc.qrcode_i18n_desc: All visible text uses i18n keys. Pass translated strings through the aria-label prop.
